skill.name: wrapped-video
skill.description: Build personalized year-in-review videos with Remotion. Use one template to turn CSV or JSON records into vertical MP4s with animated counters, ranked lists, and a final share card.
skill.summary: Turn a data table into personalized recap videos with one Remotion template.
skill.author: iart-ai

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, UI code, or expected local data handling. Unpinned CLI commands, unvalidated output IDs, and unrestricted CSS backgrounds introduce execution, overwrite, and network risks. No evidence found of prompt injection or deliberate data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Unpinned CLI commands can resolve packages at runtime.
remediation.suggestion: Declare and lock Remotion and tsx, then run installed binaries through project scripts. Do not allow automatic package downloads during rendering.

remediation.issue: Output filenames use unvalidated record IDs.
remediation.suggestion: Require unique filename-safe IDs, reject duplicates, and resolve output paths within a dedicated directory. Allow overwrites only for an explicitly approved rerun.

remediation.issue: Record data can supply an unrestricted CSS background.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only fixed palette keys or validated hex colors. Use the CSS background-color property and deny unnecessary outbound access from rendering workers.

remediation.issue: The skill names verification helpers that are absent from the reviewed package.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the unavailable helper commands or ship their reviewed implementations. Do not direct users to download substitutes at runtime.

semantic_findings.title: Unchecked Record IDs Can Overwrite Personalized Videos
semantic_findings.description: The batch examples use raw record IDs for filenames without enforcing uniqueness or output-directory containment. Duplicate IDs can overwrite another record's video, and path separators can redirect output where filesystem conditions permit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The renderer names files with the raw ID, which the shown schema does not validate. The documentation explicitly expects matching names to overwrite earlier outputs.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Accent Props Can Trigger Renderer Requests
semantic_findings.description: The schema accepts any accent string and the scene recipe assigns it to a CSS background. A background URL from a record can make a network-enabled rendering browser contact an unintended destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The schema does not enforce a color format, and the CSS background property accepts URL values. Actual reachability depends on the worker's network policy.

content.value_statement: Editing a separate recap video for every audience member takes time. Build one Remotion template and render a personalized vertical video for each data record.
actual_capabilities: Plan a five- to seven-scene recap with an intro, statistic reveals, and a final share card.
Map CSV or JSON records to a Remotion composition with a Zod schema.
Animate count-ups, ranked lists, and percentile bars using the current video frame.
Frame 1080 by 1920 videos to keep key text away from platform overlays.
Preview exact frames for a sample record, then render one MP4 per record.
limitations: You must supply per-record data and calculate any rankings or percentiles that are missing.
Rendering requires a working Node.js and Remotion project. The examples are not a complete application.
The documented verification helper scripts are not included in this package.
Cloud rendering, access controls, and video delivery require separate setup.

use_cases.title: Recap a Year of Product Use
use_cases.description: Turn approved account metrics into personalized videos for an annual customer campaign.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Vertical Recap
use_cases.description: Test ranked lists, animated counters, and a closing share card with sample records before committing to a visual design.

use_cases.title: Batch Render Member Highlights
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable render process that produces one MP4 per member from an approved data export.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a Recap
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plan a video from one sample record.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [sample record] to outline a five-scene vertical recap. Put the main statistic near the end and finish on a still share card.

prompt_templates.title: Map the Input Fields
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a dataset for a reusable template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map [CSV columns] to a Remotion props schema. Identify missing metrics and define validation rules for unique record IDs, numeric ranges, and colors.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Preview One Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: test a composition with a synthetic record.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 1080 by 1920 Remotion recap using [synthetic record]. Use frame-based animation and inspect stills at the start, main reveal, and end.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Batch Render
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: render multiple records from a reviewed dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [approved dataset] to plan a local batch render with locked tools, limited concurrency, and separate outputs. Reject duplicate IDs and verify one sample before continuing.

output_examples.input: Plan a recap for a reader who finished 28 books and read most often in October.
output: A five-scene vertical storyboard introduces the reader and shows October as the busiest month.
The main reveal counts up to 28 books. The closing frame holds that total as a still share card.

output_examples.input: Prepare a batch of recap videos from a CSV of approved membership statistics.
output: A Remotion project maps the CSV fields to reusable scenes.
Preview stills show the opening, main statistic, and closing card for a sample record.
The reviewed batch yields one vertical MP4 per valid, unique record.

best_practices: Use synthetic records for previews and public demos. Include personal details in share cards only when authorized.
Verify that the main number and ranked list match the input, then check for overlap with platform controls.
Use locked local tools, validate IDs and colors, and keep batch output in a dedicated directory.
anti_patterns: Do not batch render before checking a representative preview against its input record.
Do not use timers or random values for animation that must render consistently.
Do not use unchecked record IDs as filenames or unrestricted input strings as CSS backgrounds.

faq.question: What data do I need?
faq.answer: Provide one record per person, team, or account. Include the metrics and labels you want each scene to display.

faq.question: Does this skill use my Spotify account?
faq.answer: No. It describes a recap format and works with data you supply.

faq.question: Can I render just one recap?
faq.answer: Yes. Render one record with the same composition you would use for a full batch.

faq.question: What is the default video format?
faq.answer: The examples use a vertical 1080 by 1920 composition at 30 frames per second and export H.264 MP4 files.

faq.question: Can I check the layout before rendering the MP4?
faq.answer: Yes. Render stills at specific frames and inspect the layout and displayed values before encoding the video.

faq.question: Does the skill publish videos automatically?
faq.answer: No. The reference describes hosting options, but you must configure delivery and decide who may access each video.
